extracted.intended_audience: applicants, holders, representatives, and national/IP Offices (Contracting Parties) using the Madrid System for international trademark registration
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and Administrative Instructions governing how to prepare and file international trademark (Madrid) applications and how the International Bureau and designated Offices will process representations, communications, notifications and fees. Covers representation formats, color claims, electronic communications, provisional refusals and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single representation of the mark required
rubrics_metrics.description: As from February 1, 2023, applicants will be required to furnish only one representation of the mark in the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That single representation must be in color when the applicant claims color as a distinctive feature of the mark. The previous requirement to furnish both a black-and-white reproduction and a color reproduction (when the basic mark was in black-and-white but color is claimed) is eliminated (consequential deletion of Rule 32(1)(c)). International applications/registrations filed before Feb 1, 2023, are not affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color claim when basic mark not shown in color
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may claim color as a distinctive feature of the mark when the basic mark is protected or meant to be protected in color, even when a corresponding color claim does not appear in the basic mark and the representation of the basic mark is not in color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands prior Rule 9(4)(a)(vii) which only allowed a color claim if it appeared in the basic mark or the basic representation was in the color claimed. A claim made under this provision must also be certified by the Office of origin (see separate certification criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of origin certification for color claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall contain a declaration by the Office of origin certifying that, if color is claimed as a distinctive feature in the international application without having been claimed in the basic application/registration, the mark in the basic application/registration is in fact in the color(s) claimed, or that a corresponding color claim is included in the international application where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification requirement is reflected in Rule 9(5)(d) and clarified by amendment to Rule 9(5)(d)(v). Offices must certify conformity between the international representation and the basic mark in color-claim situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term 'reproduction' replaced by 'representation' and conformity with Administrative Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations replace the word 'reproduction' with 'representation' and require the representation of the mark to be furnished in accordance with the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequential amendments affect Rules 15(1)(iii), 17(2)(v), 32(1)(b) and item 2.1 of the Schedule of Fees. The representation requirement is therefore governed by the Administrative Instructions (including Section 11bis) rather than the former literal 'fit in the box' rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size limit for visual representations
rubrics_metrics.description: A visual representation of the mark shall not exceed a maximum size of 20 by 20 centimeters and shall be furnished in or with the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is prescribed in new Section 11bis(a) of the Administrative Instructions (20 cm length or width maximum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative single digital file for representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of a physical visual representation in or with the international application, the representation may be furnished as a single digital file accompanying the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single digital file options (Section 11bis(b)): (i) visual representation in JPEG, PNG or TIFF (per WIPO ST.67); (ii) sound recording in MP3 or WAV not exceeding 5 MB (per WIPO ST.68); (iii) motion/multimedia in MP4 with AVC/H.264 or MPEG-2/H.262 codecs not exceeding 20 MB (per WIPO ST.69). The file must comply with the relevant WIPO Standard(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Standards for electronic representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital representations must comply with the relevant WIPO Standards for electronic management of mark elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant WIPO Standards: ST.67 for figurative (visual) elements; ST.68 for sound marks; ST.69 for motion/multimedia marks. Files must meet format and technical requirements in those Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of origin certification that representation matches basic mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Rule 9(5)(d), the Office of origin must certify that the mark, as represented in or with the international application, is the same as the basic mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification remains required even where representations are furnished digitally or in color; Office must confirm identity/consistency with the basic application/registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Contracting Parties apply domestic law to protectability of non-graphical marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though the Madrid System allows international registrations for marks represented by sound, motion or multimedia recordings, designated Contracting Parties will apply their domestic legal provisions to determine whether such represented marks may be the subject of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Parties that continue to require a graphical representation of the mark might not grant protection to marks represented only by sound or motion (e.g., MP3/MP4). Applicants should consult the Madrid Member Profile for country-specific acceptability and further requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation in notification of provisional refusal (earlier mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a provisional refusal is based on an earlier mark, the notification shall contain or indicate the filing date and number, priority date (if any), registration date and number (if available), name and address of the owner, and a reproduction/representation of the former mark or an indication of how to access that representation, together with the list of relevant goods and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment to Rule 17(2)(v) gives Offices the option to provide the representation in the notification or indicate how the holder can access it (e.g., link to online database) — this is important where the earlier mark is a sound or motion recording that cannot be included in the notification itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limits and form of notifications of provisional refusal (opposition-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification of provisional refusal based on an opposition shall be confined to the elements specified in Rule 17(2) and (3) and must state concisely the grounds of the opposition (e.g., conflict with earlier mark, lack of distinctive character).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the opposition is based on a right other than a registered mark, that right (and preferably the owner) shall be identified as concisely as possible. The notification shall not be accompanied by memoranda or evidence. (See Administrative Instructions Section 15(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-documentary and non-scannable items accompanying notifications will not be recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document accompanying a notification which is not on separate sheets of A4 paper or is otherwise not suitable for scanning, and any non-documentary item such as samples or packaging, will not be recorded and will be disposed of by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is reflected in Administrative Instructions Section 15(b) (deleted paragraphs noted where postal rules changed); applicants/Offices should ensure suitable electronic/document formats are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gazette publication of representation as furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: The reproduction/representation of the mark shall be published as it was furnished in the international application; where the applicant has made the relevant declaration, the publication shall indicate that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 32(1)(b) requires publication of the representation as furnished. The prior provision requiring both black-and-white and color publication where color reproduction was furnished has been deleted (Rule 32(1)(c) deleted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic exchange of communications with the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to Section 11 prescribe that all communications with the International Bureau shall be exchanged by electronic means; communications between the International Bureau and applicants and holders may take place by electronic means in a manner to be determined by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and holders must send communications/present requests either through the Contact Madrid online platform or by using the e‑Madrid online service. Offices already exchange communications electronically. Section 11 also requires the IB to acknowledge receipt and inform originator if transmission is incomplete/unusable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of electronic transmissions and date of receipt rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall promptly inform the originator of an electronic transmission of receipt, and also advise if the transmission is incomplete or otherwise unusable, provided the originator can be identified and reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a communication is by electronic means and time-zone differences cause different sending and receipt dates, the earlier of the two dates (sending-start or receipt-of-complete-communication) shall be considered the date of receipt by the International Bureau (Section 11(b) and (c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for applicants/holders/representatives to provide e-mail addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Holders and their representatives should have an e-mail address on record and benefit from receiving electronic communications; those who have not yet indicated an e-mail address must do so without delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As the International Bureau continues to deliver secure online services, holders/representatives without an e-mail address will find it increasingly difficult to manage international registrations. The IB will send electronic acknowledgements and communications to the address on record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation required for date of international registration (irregularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application received by the International Bureau does not contain a representation of the mark (among other required elements), that irregularity affects the date of the international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 15(1)(iii) lists the representation of the mark as an element needed to avoid irregularity affecting the date; applicants must ensure the representation is properly furnished per the Administrative Instructions to secure the correct date of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees: higher basic fee when any representation is in color
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic fee for an international application differs depending on whether any representation of the mark is in color: 653 CHF where no representation is in color; 903 CHF where any representation is in color (as in force on Feb 1, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applicants from Least Developed Countries (per UN list), the basic fee is reduced to 10% of the prescribed amount (65 CHF where no representation is in color; 90 CHF where any representation is in color). The Schedule of Fees text was amended to reflect 'representation' wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of postal rules and paper-multiple-documents rule due to electronic communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Section 11 prescribes electronic exchange with the International Bureau, Section 6(b) (several documents mailed in one envelope), Section 14 (date of sending of notifications via postal services), and Section 15(b) (documents accompanying a notification of provisional refusal) have been deleted or modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural postal provisions are removed; parties should use electronic platforms (Contact Madrid/e-Madrid). Where prior postal-date rules applied, consult Information Notice No. 19/2022 for transition guidance.
